agency: Washington State Criminal Justice Training Commission
criminal_detail: No criminal charges were reported. LeLand Allen resigned from the Port of Seattle Police Department in 2023 in lieu of termination, and the Washington State Criminal Justice Training Commission issued a formal statement of administrative charges against him in December 2024.
incident_date_approx: 2021-2022 (Basic Law Enforcement Academy Class 828, which graduated February 2022)
description: Snohomish County sheriff's Deputy Haydyn Wagner and Port Orchard police Officer Aimee Allen filed a lawsuit on October 13, 2023 against the Washington State Criminal Justice Training Commission and Port of Seattle police Officer LeLand Allen, who served as a 'Training, Advising, Counseling' officer at the state's Basic Law Enforcement Academy. The suit alleges Allen used his position to sexually harass and touch female recruits of academy Class 828, including placing his hands inside tears in one plaintiff's jeans during a training scenario and tapping the other plaintiff's buttocks while commenting on her body. According to the complaint, all six female cadets in the class complained about Allen, and an independent workplace investigation concluded a preponderance of the evidence supported the allegations. Allen resigned from the Port of Seattle Police Department in 2023 in lieu of termination, and the state commission issued administrative charges against him in December 2024. No settlement, judgment, or dismissal of this lawsuit has been found in available reporting.
notes: Outside strict police-department definition (state law-enforcement training commission; accused trainer was a Port of Seattle Police Department officer). Companion to rec-66 (Ricksecker suit, April 2024, different trainer at the same academy); this was the first of the academy sexual-harassment suits.
